bias: 'Buyers take control, but vulnerable structure and major overhead resistance leave the door open for sellers.' Wednesday finally delivered the missing upside initiative: both opened on substantial true gaps, defended the opening inventory correction and broke their IB highs, leaving bullish RTH gaps (NQ: Tue high 28090 → Wed low 28199, between 28080-28100 and 28200-28233; ES: Tue high 7566.25 → Wed low 7593.25, with Wed's low ≈ Monday's high 7600.5). The short-term trend belongs to buyers — but the HTF bearish trend is not defeated: NQ is still inside last week's range with the 29K test (28944-28969 / 29038-29069) waiting, ES is still inside Thursday's mother bar and closed just under 7645-7650 with unfinished business at 7670-7680. Wednesday's relatively light volume isn't bearish by itself but leaves parts of the new structure vulnerable if aggressive sellers return. 'Until and unless sellers can establish traction below a prior day's low, bulls remain in control of the short-term trend' — don't chase longs into resistance, but require sellers to prove control before treating an upside rejection as a reversal.
wildcard: Sellers 'need to pitch a shutout': their first step is the prior day's low with continuation; the second is filling the bullish RTH gap and accepting back inside Tuesday's range. NQ can consolidate between Wed's high and RTH low without being bearish as long as the gap is broadly protected. Globex reopened sharply lower at 18:00 (ES ~7607-7619, NQ ~28156-28306 — single bar, verify): NQ already inside its gap, ES sitting on Mon high / Wed low. Daily: ES 7663-7664, 7633-7636, 7562-7563; NQ 29194-29220, 27869, 27689, 27110-27123.
